title: feat(security): server.trustProxy gains a trusted-network form; the client address is read from the trusted hop
body:
Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: added
Skills-docs: none — no skill under `skills/**` teaches `server.trustProxy` or forwarded headers; `docs/HARDENING.md`, `content/docs/deployment/production-readiness.mdx`, `content/docs/protocol/kernel/http-protocol.mdx` and `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx` gain the form in this change.

## 维护者速读

- 部署在反向代理后的运维,现在可以在服务器配置里列出自己的代理网段;服务器只信这些代理转发来的客户端地址,登录审计、IP 白名单和限流都按这个地址判断。
- 为什么做:按维护者本轮裁定落地「可信网段」写法,并让旧的「全部信任」写法在可疑请求出现时提醒一次。
- 出错会怎样:写错的网段在启动时就被拒绝并点名;旧写法行为不变,只多一条提醒;改动可整体撤回。
- 要你做什么:无。

## What changes

The hardening rule: **the client address is read from the trusted hop.**

- `server.trustProxy` (`packages/spec`, `StackServerConfigSchema`) accepts a third form beside `false` and `true`: `{ networks, header }` (`TrustedProxyNetworksSchema`). `networks` lists the addresses or CIDR ranges of the deployment's reverse proxies; `header` is `'x-forwarded-for'` (default) or `'x-real-ip'`. A malformed entry, an empty list, an unknown header and an unknown key are refused at authoring.
- The one client-address rule (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/client-address.ts`, `resolveClientAddress`) reads that form: a forwarded header is believed only on a connection whose peer is inside `networks`; `X-Forwarded-For` is then read from the right, past every hop inside `networks`, and the first entry outside them is the client. `X-Real-IP` is read only when the form names it. Several header lines are read as one list, under every form.
- `readTrustProxy` (same module, exported on `@objectstack/plugin-auth/client-address`) is the one reading of the declaration. Every former `trustProxy === true` reader now reads through it, so the new form reaches every consumer: `AuthManager` (D5 allow-list, D7 `last_login_ip`, the vendored library's address), the runtime's inbound rate limiter and per-endpoint limiter (`dispatcher-plugin.ts`, `security/inbound-rate-limit.ts`, `endpoint-policy.ts`), and `objectstack serve`, which hands the authored value to both `AuthPlugin` and the dispatcher as it is. A malformed form is refused at boot, naming the entry.
- Under `server.trustProxy: true`, behaviour is unchanged, and a once-per-process `warn` (not `error`) fires the first time an `X-Forwarded-For` with more than one entry arrives, naming the trusted-network form. The latch lives on `globalThis` under a registered symbol, because the module is bundled into more than one entry (`splitting: false`).
- Both ADR-0069 D5 operator warnings in `auth-plugin.ts`, and the inbound limiter's "cannot identify anonymous callers" warning, now say that `true` needs a proxy that overwrites `X-Forwarded-For` and never appends to it, and they name the trusted-network form.
- The address and range parser the D5 allow-list uses moved, unchanged, from `auth-manager.ts` into a new import-free internal module `ip-range.ts`, so the lean `./client-address` entry can match a range exactly as the allow-list does. `auth-manager.ts` re-exports `parseIpRange`, `ipMatchesRange`, `unreadableIpRangeEntries` and `IpRange`, so the package root keeps its surface.
- Docs: `docs/HARDENING.md`, `content/docs/deployment/production-readiness.mdx`, `content/docs/protocol/kernel/http-protocol.mdx`, `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`. Regenerated spec artifacts (`api-surface/`, `export-origins/`, `declaration-map/`, `authorable-surface/`, `authorable-defaults/`, `json-schema.manifest/`, `content/docs/references/**`, the strictness ledger counts).

Order of record: the maintainer ruling, verbatim: "**Maintainer ruling (os-justin, 2026-11-17, in the security#2 session): the trusted-network form this release; `true` refused from the next major.**" This PR is this release's half only.

Read first, by risk:

1. `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/client-address.ts` — `believedFromTrustedNetworks` (the right-to-left walk) and `readTrustProxy`.
2. `packages/runtime/src/dispatcher-plugin.ts` — the one `readTrustProxy` call at plugin creation, shared by both limiters.
3. `packages/spec/src/system/stack-server.zod.ts` — `TrustedProxyNetworksSchema` and the `trustProxy` union.

## Tests

New and extended pins, each red on the base and green here:

- `plugin-auth/src/client-address.test.ts` (new, 18): the right-to-left walk past declared hops; control: one declared proxy reporting a client; a peer outside `networks` believed for nothing; X-Real-IP only when named; IPv6 networks and IPv4-mapped peers; several header lines merged (both forms); `true` and `false` unchanged; the once-per-process warning (fires once, multi-line counts, a sink-less consumer does not spend it, never under the trusted-network form or `false`); `readTrustProxy` accept/refuse.
- `plugin-auth/src/client-ip-allow-list-trust-rule.test.ts` (+4, real Hono mount + real `AuthManager`): the allow-list judges the entry the declared proxy appended (control admitted, `403 IP_NOT_ALLOWED` on the other); a peer outside `networks` judged itself; `last_login_ip` records the appended entry; `AuthManager` reads the form and refuses a malformed one at construction.
- `runtime/src/security/inbound-rate-limit.test.ts` (+4), `runtime/src/endpoint-policy.test.ts` (+1), `runtime/src/dispatcher-plugin.rate-limit.integration.test.ts` (+2, a real server over a socket): each reader keys by the appended entry under the form; malformed forms refused at build; the `true` warning reaches the limiter's logger once.
- `cli/src/commands/serve-trust-proxy.contract.test.ts` (new, 3): `serve.ts` narrows no `trustProxy` reading to a boolean and hands both consumers the authored value; both consumers read the form.
- `spec/src/system/stack-server.test.ts` (+6): accept the form (header defaulted), `true`/`false` still accepted, reachable from `defineStack`, refuse empty/missing `networks`, a bad entry, an unknown header, an unknown key.

## Acceptance notes

- **Owed for the next major (not in this PR):** `server.trustProxy: true` is refused at boot, with a migration entry, per the same ruling. Until then a deployment that keeps `true` behind a proxy that appends to `X-Forwarded-For` keeps the leftmost-entry reading, and is told once per process.
- `X-Forwarded-For` entries carrying a port (`203.0.113.7:51234`, as some load balancers write them) are not addresses to the trusted-network form: a trusted hop reporting one establishes no address (the limiter keys `ip:unknown`, the allow-list refuses). Not seen in the repo's own deployments; a follow-up if a host needs it.
- Under the trusted-network form, a peer outside `networks` that sends a forwarded header is judged itself, and the D5 "header not believed" operator warning does not fire for it (that warning is written for an undeclared `trustProxy`). A misdeclared network is therefore quiet today.
- `GET /admin/client-address` and `GET /client-address` still answer `trustProxy` as a boolean ("forwarded headers counted"), true under either declared form; the wire shape is unchanged.
- The per-endpoint limiter's wiring in `dispatcher-plugin.ts` reads the same `readTrustProxy` constant as the server limiter; its behaviour under the form is pinned at `endpoint-policy.test.ts`, not through a booted endpoint.
- ADR-0069's D5 note (client-address mechanism) is not amended here; `docs/adr/**` is a governed surface, so that line is the owning seat's.
- `Metadata-protocol: added` ⇒ `@objectstack/spec` ships `minor` (AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3); the other three packages ship `patch`.
- Contract-tier review of this PR is the security seat's.
